title: 7J quiz with answer key
subject: Science
source: Seeded from science/y7 lesson 40 (7J quiz with answer key (portal))
intro: Covers lessons 32 to 49 of Current electricity (7J); forces (7K). Answer every question. For multiple choice, fill in one circle.

questions.q: Which circuit lights the lamp?
options: Lamp and closed switch, no cell
questions.a: B) Cell, lamp, closed switch. Only a complete circuit with a cell lets current flow.

questions.q: An ammeter reads 0.4 A before a lamp. After the lamp it reads...
questions.a: B) 0.4 A. Current is not used up in a series circuit.

questions.q: In the rope model, what is the cell?
questions.a: B) The person pulling. The cell pushes the charge, like the puller drives the rope.

questions.q: Total 1.2 A splits into two equal branches. Each branch carries...
questions.a: A) 0.6 A. Branches share the total: 1.2 ÷ 2 = 0.6 A.

questions.q: Three 1.5 V cells in series give...
questions.a: C) 4.5 V. Cell voltages in series add: 3 × 1.5 = 4.5 V.

questions.q: 9 V across a resistor, 3 A through it. R = ?
questions.a: A) 3 Ω. R = V ÷ I = 9 ÷ 3 = 3 Ω. 27 comes from multiplying by mistake.

questions.q: Why is the fuse in the live wire?
options: When it melts the appliance is cut off from the high voltage
questions.a: B) When it melts the appliance is cut off from the high voltage. Breaking the live connection makes the appliance safe.

questions.q: A 1.5 kW oven runs for 2 hours. Energy used?
questions.a: B) 3 kWh. kWh = kW × h = 1.5 × 2 = 3 kWh.

questions.q: Three branches: 0.2 A, 0.2 A, 0.4 A. Supply current?
questions.a: B) 0.8 A. Branch currents add: 0.2 + 0.2 + 0.4 = 0.8 A.

questions.q: A 50 kg pupil's weight on Earth?
Spring extends 1.5 cm for 1 N. For 3 N (below the limit)?
questions.a: C) 4.5 cm. Proportional: 3 × 1.5 = 4.5 cm.

questions.q: Which reading is most likely an anomaly: 1.1, 2.0, 3.2, 4.0 cm at 1 to 4 N?
questions.a: B) 3.2. The pattern is about 1 cm per N, so 3.2 sits furthest off the trend.

questions.q: Which reduces drag on a cyclist?
options: Sitting upright with a big coat
questions.a: B) Crouching low. A low, streamlined shape lets air flow past more easily.

questions.q: Same 500 N force on 0.5 m² or 0.05 m². Which has the higher pressure?
questions.a: B) 0.05 m². Smaller area, higher pressure: 10 000 N/m² against 1000 N/m².

questions.q: Which made the deepest print?
questions.a: C) Tin rim. Smallest area, highest pressure (2.0 N/cm²), deepest print.

questions.q: Forward 200 N, backward 200 N, moving. It will...
questions.a: C) Keep the same speed. Balanced forces: resultant 0, so no change in motion.

questions.q: Which increases thinking distance?
questions.a: A) A tired driver. Tiredness slows reactions; the others affect braking distance.

questions.q: Which unit is pressure?
questions.a: B) N/m². Pressure is force per area.

questions.q: The arrangement of particles in a solid is...
questions.a: Close together in a regular pattern
options: Close together in a regular pattern

questions.q: Which organ system includes the heart?
questions.a: Circulatory system
